The part that goes wrong is not the sending: it is sending the same email twice, or not at all, when rows get sorted, edited or deleted. This guide contains affiliate links, marked “affiliate link”. Keep uncertain outcomes for inspection before releasing a row again. Before enabling the scenario, inspect the destination using a fictional input and compare the result with the intended business outcome. Key facts Select only rows deliberately marked ready.

articles.title: Title: Converting RecallOS into a Terminal-Based Local AI Document Assistant
articles.excerpt: RecallOS is a Python-based AI document memory and search assistant built using Streamlit, Ollama, and ChromaDB. I want to convert it into a terminal-only application that runs directly inside VS Code…
articles.body: RecallOS is a Python-based AI document memory and search assistant built using Streamlit, Ollama, and ChromaDB. I want to convert it into a terminal-only application that runs directly inside VS Code without opening a browser. The application should support PDF, DOCX, TXT, and Markdown documents. It should extract text from documents and generate embeddings using Sentence Transformers. ChromaDB should store document embeddings and support semantic search. Ollama with Gemma 3 (4B) should generate answers locally using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The application should display relevant source documents and passages alongside answers. It should preserve local chat history and allow users to search previous conversations.

How Font Rendering Works in Browsers Browsers render text using the OS text rendering stack plus their own adjustments: Windows : DirectWrite (since Firefox 36) — uses ClearType for sub-pixel rendering on LCD screens macOS : CoreText — Apple's font rendering, same as Safari uses Linux : FreeType + Fontconfig, with optional sub-pixel rendering Firefox gives you more explicit control over this than Chrome does.

articles.body: By Isaac Muthui, CEO, Tamalaki Business Network Ltd. Originally published at factoraerp.com . In food manufacturing ERPs, dispatch is often modelled as "create delivery note → reduce stock." That model fails the moment a held pallet looks identical to a released one, or FEFO loses to "whatever was nearest the door." The operational risk is not forgetting to print a DN. It is letting a status machine lie: WarehouseHold stock riding out on a DispatchOrder that should only allocate Released lots. articles.title: Checking Whether a Backlink Actually Fits: A Small Python Script
articles.excerpt: If you build sites for clients, sooner or later someone hands you a list of backlinks they've paid for and asks, "are these any good?" Metrics tools will give you a number. What they won't tell you qu…
articles.body: If you build sites for clients, sooner or later someone hands you a list of backlinks they've paid for and asks, "are these any good?" Metrics tools will give you a number. What they won't tell you quickly is whether each link fits the page it points to. At Unfair Links we spend a lot of time on that question, because our whole approach is matching links to the country, language and niche of a specific page. This post shares a stripped-down version of the kind of first-pass check you can run yourself. It's not magic, and it won't replace a human looking at the page, but it catches the obvious mismatches in seconds. What we're checking For each linking page, we want to know four things: Is the link actually there? Pages get edited, links get removed. Is it crawlable?

articles.title: It's time to reassess the size of our solar system, scientists say
articles.excerpt: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system based on the Milky Way's gravity, including its dark matter.
articles.body: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system by presenting a theory which states that measurements of the Milky Way's gravitational field, including its dark matter, redraws the sun's frontier. That theory was put forward by Jim Green, former NASA chief scientist and past director of the space agency's Planetary Science Division, along with Ed Belbruno, a professor of mathematics at Yeshiva University and a senior research associate at Princeton University. The solar system's gravitational frontier extends to nearly 3.8 light-years from the sun , they contend, roughly 241,000 astronomical units (AU), a distance that brings the "edge" of the solar system to within the same scale as the separation between neighboring stars.

articles.title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
articles.excerpt: The incident is likely 1st confirmation of mercenary spyware delivered by targeted ads.
articles.body: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app. The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software.
articles.author: Dan Goodin

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long his…
articles.body: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars’ orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background.
